A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same code-mixing benchmark and synthesis pipeline. The text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–J support reliable comparison despite renaming and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations in Tables 2 and 8, k-shot experiments, and synthetic-data validation results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, k-shot experiments, and synthetic-data validation results, including those in the appendices.

M1.justification: The GPT-4 Turbo word-substitution pipeline, automatic language annotation, and word-level, semantic, and model-aligned filtering remain unchanged. The synthesis prompts in Appendix F are retained; CodeMixEval is renamed CodeMixBench.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 22 synthetic and 30 collected datasets, covering eight tasks and 18 languages. The dataset descriptions, language pairs, and task coverage in Section 3 and Appendices A–B and H are retained.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same 13 GPT, LLaMA, and Mistral/Mixtral configurations. Table 8 retains the same four GPT comparators for the traditional NLP tasks; no evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Figure 2 and Table 8 relabel NER evaluation from accuracy to F1. However, Section 4.1 still specifies accuracy and the scores remain identical, so the PDFs do not establish recalculation. Other evaluation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The cross-language analysis, k-shot sensitivity experiments, manual synthesis checks, validation examples, and mixing-index distributions are retained in Sections 4.3–4.4 and Appendices D–E and H–J. No new ablation or robustness analysis appears.

E5.justification: Both report point scores and averages without repeated-run uncertainty, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The human-review sampling and MAPE-based agreement calculation in Appendices D–E are unchanged.

E6.justification: The matched tables and plots retain their numerical results, rankings, and trends. For example, Table 2 retains GPT-4o's 80.97 average on CM-MMLU and GPT-4 Turbo's 93.42 on CM-GSM8K. NER values are unchanged despite the metric relabeling.

T1.justification: The M-index and I-index definitions in Section 3.4 and MAPE/agreement formulas in Appendix E are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: v1's 'most extensive analytical framework' becomes the 'first comprehensive benchmark.' v2 also explicitly claims the first integration of word substitution with LLM prompts and emphasizes synthesis efficiency. The coverage and principal empirical claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The limitations retain data-quality concerns but remove explicit regional coverage gaps and the explanation that synthesis costs constrain language and task diversity. v2 adds discussion of multilingual quality control and potential bias mitigation. The main result interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-and-dataset availability statement and repository link in the abstract. Existing prompts, tokenization instructions, decoding parameters, and the synthesis cost reported in Appendix H are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ravfogel et al. (2020) and Peng et al. (2025) for bias mitigation, condenses criticism of prior synthesis approaches, and removes the favorable description of Yong et al.'s zero-shot generation findings. The broader related-work coverage is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are rewritten and condensed around the benchmark framing, and terminology is standardized to CodeMixBench. The title, author affiliation/contact, and acknowledgments change, while the overall section and appendix structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 swaps the SA and NER panels and adds an F1 axis label; Table 8 changes the NER heading accordingly. Existing figures are relocated, including Figure 4 before the references and Figure 5 alongside Appendix H text. No new figure or table is added.

improvement.justification: Clearer benchmark framing and new code/data access information improve usability. However, the NER relabeling introduces a conflict with Section 4.1, and specific coverage and cost limitations disappear without corresponding experimental changes. These benefits and reporting weaknesses leave the net effect on overall quality uncertain.
